newsitem.title: USA: MetLife unit buys real estate firm - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: MetLife unit buys real estate firm - WSJ.

text.p: A unit of Metropolitan Life Insurance has agreed to acquire a real-estate advisory firm called Aldrich, Eastman & Waltch for more than $70 million, the Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday.

The newspaper cited "people familiar with the transaction" as saying New England Investment Co, 55 percent of which is owns by MetLife, could pay $35 million more for the firm depending on its performance over time.
It said the unit, which was expected to announce the deal as soon as Tuesday, would merge the firm with its own Copley Real Estate Advisors.
The new advisory firm, to be called AEW Capital Management, would manage assets worth a total of about $7.6 billion, it added.
